correctness.rationale: The stationary renewal identity gives A~Exp(r) and an exact bivariate Gaussian free excursion. The covariance expressions follow by integrating independent Brownian covariances. The positive-X tail integral has a unique nondegenerate saddle at a sqrt(x) with curvature 4r/a; uniform Gaussian tail bounds give the sharp marginal prefactor and Gaussian age fluctuations. Gaussian path regression plus uniform residual maximal bounds gives the polynomial paths. Endpoint regression yields independent Gaussian residual variance Da/2 and age-induced contribution Da/4, giving total 3Da/4 and correlation -sgn(gamma)/sqrt(3). Standalone reproducibility code passed 177 kernel and quadrature assertions; finite tests are not used to prove the infinite threshold limit.

originality.rationale: Against available primary full texts and searches, no previously established result was found providing the joint stationary Poisson-reset age and transverse endpoint CLT with parameter-free correlation magnitude 1/sqrt(3). The source 2024 shear-reset article covers the exact model, Gaussian propagator and steady-state moments. Singh 2020 already covers the integrated-Brownian reset stationary density and its stretched-exponential marginal tail. Meerson 2023 already obtains the complementary cubic optimal bridge in a different first-passage setting. Neither isolated tail nor cubic is credited as new. Existing mixture formulas could imply the result after additional analysis, so independent scholarly priority review remains necessary.
residual_risks: Known renewal-mixture and Gaussian regression machinery may make the asserted limit a latent consequence of a more general Gaussian-mixture conditional theorem not located in this review.
The isolated stretched-exponential tail and complementary cubic are covered by older random-acceleration work and are not credited independently.
Priority has not been independently audited. No finite-threshold error bound, no uniformity near zero shear, and no sample-based inference claim.

value.rationale: A rare longitudinal excursion has a nontrivial time history: its backward age fluctuates on x^(1/4), its transverse endpoint is a different Gaussian fluctuation, and their signed correlation approaches a nonobvious universal magnitude 1/sqrt(3), while the conditioned full trajectory has specified geometry. This provides a physically interpretable cross-coordinate rare-event benchmark beyond mean/variance/skewness measurements in the motivating shear-reset model. The precise value is motivated by indirect estimation of the reset-free residence history from spatial observations. It does not depend on a claim that routine marginal tails or Gaussian-bridge polynomials are new.
